title: Parallel Recording
hook: You're not forgetful. You're just using your brain as a to-do list.
statement: Get things out of your head and into a system you trust.
explainer: Every task you hold in memory keeps running in the background, draining focus. Writing it down once closes that loop and frees up room to think.
sop: Capture every task and idea the second it shows up, in one inbox.
Count your open Tasks and how many live in External Aids.
Review the inbox daily: do it, schedule it, or file it.
Never let a captured item live only in your memory.
Trust the system and stop mentally rehearsing it.
equation_example: 20 open Tasks, 15 captured in External Aids. 20 - 15 = 5 things still rattling around your head. Lower means more room for real thinking. Higher means you're spending focus on remembering instead of doing.
question: Write down every open loop in your head right now, then put them all in one place.
closing_statement: Capture it once and it stops costing you twice.
caption:
Principle Nº 223: Parallel Recording

You're not forgetful. You're just using your brain as a to-do list.

Get things out of your head and into a system you trust.
